transcript.content: Hi, welcome in. I'm Dr. [Name]. To start, can you tell me what brings you in to see me today?
What finally scared me enough to come in is... I keep thinking it would be a relief if I just didn’t wake up. I haven’t tried to hurt myself, but those thoughts have been there.
How long have you been feeling this way—having these thoughts and low mood—has it been days, weeks, or longer?
About four months now. It started around when my aunt came to live with us.
Over these four months, would you say you've felt down or lost interest in things nearly every day, for most of the day, or does it come and go depending on what's happening with your aunt?
Most mornings I wake up with this heavy sadness in my chest, like I’ve already failed the day before the day even starts.

Do you notice this heavy sadness and lack of interest even during times when you're away from your aunt or not dealing with issues related to her, or does it mainly show up in connection with that situation?
It’s there even when nothing’s going on with my aunt. Most mornings I wake up with this heavy sadness in my chest, like I’ve already failed before the day even starts.
Have you ever had a period like this before—weeks or months of similarly low mood and loss of interest—at any other time in your life, prior to these last four months?
I’m not really sure. I can’t think of another time that lasted weeks or months like this.

Over these past four months, how much have these feelings affected your ability to go to work, take care of yourself, or keep up with daily responsibilities—are you still managing most tasks, or has it become very difficult to function at all?
It’s gotten harder. I’ve stopped going to my dance class, the walking group, and my food-pantry shifts. My husband’s been doing more of the errands because I get stuck and fall behind.
When you have those thoughts about not waking up, have you thought about how you might do it, or made any plans, or is it more a general wish to escape the pain without a specific plan?
It’s more like wishing I just wouldn’t wake up. I haven’t tried to hurt myself. That thought is what scared me enough to come in.
Right now, are you still able to manage basic daily activities like getting dressed, eating, and looking after yourself, or has it become nearly impossible to do even those things most days?

I can still manage the basic things, mostly. But I’ve stopped doing the things I used to do, like dance class and the walking group, and I haven’t been going to the food pantry. My husband’s had to take over more errands because I get stuck and fall behind.
Are you still able to go to work and complete your job duties, or has your depression made it very difficult to function there as well?
I’m not working now. But I have stopped going to my dance class, the walking group, and my food-pantry shifts. My husband’s been taking over more errands because I get stuck and fall behind.
Have you noticed significant changes in your sleep or appetite over these past four months—such as trouble falling or staying asleep, or eating much more or less than usual?
I’m not really sure I’ve noticed a big change in either one.
On the hardest days, do you find yourself unable to get out of bed, bathe, or care for yourself at all, or are you still able to do these things even if it takes extra effort?

I can still do the basic things, but it takes more effort. I’ve mostly stopped going to my dance class, the walking group, and the food-pantry shifts, and my husband has had to take over more errands because I get stuck and fall behind.
